summary: Across the week, global trade signals pointed to temporary diplomatic stabilization—highlighted by US-China tariff relief agreements and a extended trade truce alongside an evolving India-China political thaw—even as critical maritime choke-points faced persistent security threats. Unrest in the Red Sea and expanding conflict risks into the Indian Ocean continue to disrupt ocean freight routes, elevating seafarer risks and driving up tanker values despite volatile crude prices. In response, major Asian economies are aggressively accelerating investments in automated port infrastructure, alternative overland corridors, and green maritime infrastructure to build long-term supply chain resilience against ongoing geopolitical vulnerabilities.
